questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the core difference between data classification and a control like a Validation Rule or Platform Encryption?
options: There is no difference; classification is itself a type of Validation Rule
Classification is a labeling step that identifies sensitivity so the right controls can be deliberately chosen; Validation Rules and encryption are controls that actively act on data
Classification always runs after encryption is already configured
Classification only applies to standard fields, never custom fields
questions.explain: Classification is the labeling step that precedes and informs the choice of active controls -- it doesn't itself block a save or encrypt anything.

questions.q: Which native Salesforce field-level metadata attribute records which regulation (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, PCI) makes a given field relevant?
options: Field Usage
Data Owner
Compliance Categorization
Data Sensitivity Level
questions.explain: Compliance Categorization records which regulation applies to a field (commonly including options like PII, GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA, PCI), distinct from Data Sensitivity Level, which records how sensitive the content is.

questions.q: Why does this lesson stress that Data Sensitivity Level and Compliance Categorization are "metadata tags, not a content scanner"?
options: Because setting a field's classification is a human decision recorded as metadata -- it doesn't inspect the field's actual data, and tagging a field Restricted doesn't by itself change any Salesforce behavior
Because these fields can only be set by Salesforce support, never by admins
Because metadata tags are automatically removed after 90 days
Because classification tags are visible only to the record's owner
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that classifying a field this way records a human judgment as metadata and does not itself trigger any automatic encryption, hiding, or auditing -- enforcement is a separate step.

questions.q: What role does Data Detect (a Shield capability) play, per this lesson, relative to the four native classification metadata fields?
options: Data Detect automatically sets the final classification with no human review needed
Data Detect scans for sensitive-data patterns at scale to surface candidate fields for a human to review and formally classify -- it's a discovery tool, not a decision-maker
Data Detect replaces the need for Compliance Categorization entirely
Data Detect only works on objects that have zero existing classification tags
questions.explain: Data Detect finds likely sensitive fields using pattern matching, but the actual classification decision is still made by a human (the data owner, informed by a steward) reviewing what it surfaces.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when does a data classification program actually deliver value?
options: The moment every field in the org has a classification tag applied, regardless of what happens next
Only once something downstream -- an encryption rollout, an access review, an audit response -- actually reads the classification labels and acts on them
Classification programs never deliver measurable value in a Salesforce context
Only after the org disables Data Classification Settings
questions.explain: The lesson states a classification program with no downstream consumer of its labels is busywork -- the payoff comes from wiring the labels into real decisions like encryption or access review scope.
